clue.text: Opportunity to buy duty-free French perfume, new in, getting it in the box

indicators.note: in here means placed inside, so the letter sits within the perfume name

parts.note: Chanel is the Parisian fashion and fragrance house
N is the standard abbreviation for new
in football, putting the ball into the penalty box from the wing is a cross

explanation.surface: A shopper hunts for cheap French scent on the ferry, stuffing a bottle into a box.
explanation.walkthrough: The N goes inside CHANEL; the second half is a cryptic football reading of 'getting it in the box'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferry and tunnel passengers between England and France traditionally stocked up at tax-free shops on board.

clue.text: One responsible for numerous shootings?

parts.note: surface reading: a gunman or serial killer
setter's reading: shooting is filming scenes, so this is the person in charge of the camera work on a film

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'shootings' is meant in its film-set sense rather than with guns.
explanation.definitionFit: The director of photography on a movie oversees every camera take, which the trade calls shooting.

clue.text: Consultant initially against deploying face mask

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the leading letters of these two words
a visor is a shield worn over the face

explanation.surface: An adviser who at first opposed rolling out face coverings in a pandemic.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisor, the American spelling of adviser, is a person consulted for expert guidance.

clue.text: Inquisitive about leader of Conservatives and cocaine

indicators.note: about means going around, so the inquisitive word wraps the other letters

parts.note: nosey means prying or curious

indicators.note: 'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Conservatives'

parts.note: first letter of Conservatives
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journalist digging into a Tory leader's drug use.
explanation.definitionFit: Nose candy is slang for the powdered drug, since it is snorted up the nose.

clue.text: Playful daughter opens sluice after wiping walls

indicators.note: wiping the walls of something clears off its outermost letters at each end
opens here means splits apart and sits inside

parts.note: sluice with its outer letters stripped
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A cheerful girl opens the sluice gate after scrubbing the walls down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludic is a formal adjective from Latin ludus, game, meaning showing spontaneous play.

clue.text: Copy cat enters answers not fully completed

indicators.note: something not fully completed stops short, losing its final letter
to enter is to go inside, so the animal sits within the other word

parts.note: replies, cut short at the end
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheat copies answers while a cat wanders over the half-finished exam paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To replicate is to make an exact duplicate, as with an experiment repeated.

clue.text: Broke family thrown into street

indicators.note: something thrown into a place ends up inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
kin are one's relatives

explanation.surface: A penniless family evicted onto the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is everyday British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Broke and skint are both informal adjectives for being out of money.

clue.text: As a normal pregnancy, minutes from being discovered?

indicators.note: discovered means having the cover removed, so both words lose their outer letters

parts.note: minutes stripped of its first and last letters
from stripped of its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pregnancy only minutes away from being found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being discovered' applies to both preceding words; the answer is split 2,5 but built 5,2.
explanation.definitionFit: In utero is Latin for inside the womb, which is where a typical pregnancy develops.

clue.text: Salute guard at sea carrying older lady — that's sweet!

indicators.note: at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
gran is short for grandmother

explanation.surface: Sailors salute a guard of honour as a grandmother is carried aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carrying' joins the two parts of the anagram fodder; all fifteen letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Granulated sugar is ordinary table sweetener in small grains, so it is literally a sweet thing.

clue.text: All Saints' day: miserable Serbian city

parts.note: All Saints' Day falls on 1 November, written NOV I
sad means unhappy

explanation.surface: A gloomy holy day spent in a dreary Serbian town.
explanation.walkthrough: The date is written with the month abbreviation and a Roman numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Novi Sad is Serbia's second-largest city, on the Danube.

clue.text: Formal uniform lightened at the front with a flower

parts.note: prim means stiffly proper

indicators.note: at the front keeps only the leading letter of each word it governs

parts.note: first letters of these two words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Formal dress brightened up at the front with a flower pinned on.
explanation.definitionFit: Primula is the plant genus that includes primroses and cowslips.

clue.text: Erasmus iconically bestrides this art form

indicators.note: to bestride is to stand astride, so the letters straddle the gap between two words

parts.note: the tail of the first word and the head of the second

explanation.surface: The great Renaissance scholar towers over this art like an icon.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is the art of organised sound, one of the classic fine arts.

clue.text: Poor reaction by United; they bottle it in France

indicators.note: a poor version of something is botched, so the letters come out badly arranged

parts.note: the word's letters rearranged
U is the abbreviation for United in football team names

explanation.surface: A football club's players lose their nerve in a European tie in France.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'bottle it' is British slang for losing your nerve; in the definition it literally means putting liqueur in bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is both an orange liqueur and the French company in Angers that makes and bottles it.

clue.text: Hairy brute first to attend rave in Oklahoma city, second to leave

indicators.note: in places the other letters inside the city name
the second letter of the city name is dropped out

parts.note: Tulsa is the second city of Oklahoma
to rave is to rant wildly

indicators.note: first to keeps only the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: opening letter of attend

explanation.surface: A big ugly bloke is the first to show up at a party in Tulsa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second to leave' refers to the city's own second letter, the S, which drops out once the other letters are inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarantula is a large spider covered with bristles, a fearsome beast to arachnophobes.

clue.text: Peacekeepers under attack left boxed in without a strategy

parts.note: United Nations troops keep the peace

indicators.note: something boxed in is enclosed on all sides by the surrounding letters

parts.note: panned means harshly criticised
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: UN troops, ambushed and trapped, have no plan of action.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done with no plan or strategy behind it is unplanned.

clue.text: Behold one getting advanced instrument

indicators.note: the letter for one is moved forward a place, a small rearrangement of the word

parts.note: voila is French for look, there it is, and it contains the letter for one

explanation.surface: Look, someone has been given a more advanced instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the I moves, forward one position, in the borrowed French exclamation.
explanation.definitionFit: The viola is the stringed instrument a little larger than the violin.

clue.text: Champion Scotsman from the late 19th century?

parts.note: a victor is a winner
Ian is a typical Scottish first name

explanation.surface: A Scottish champion athlete of the 1890s.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the fact that the Victorian era ran from 1837 to 1901, not only the late part of the century.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Victoria reigned until 1901, so anything of that era is Victorian.

clue.text: One set to catch Flashman according to a ventriloquist?

indicators.note: a ventriloquist cannot move the lips, so lip sounds like B get swapped for G, as in gottle of geer

parts.note: Flashman is the bully in Tom Brown's Schooldays; that word said without moving the lips

explanation.surface: A ventriloquist's act features a fielder poised to catch the villain Flashman.
explanation.walkthrough: Gully is a cricket fielding position close to the batsman on the off side, placed to take catches.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielder at that cricket position is stationed specifically to take edged catches.

clue.text: Non-explicit quality of 10 with frilly clothing

indicators.note: clothing wraps around, so the number is dressed inside the frilly word

parts.note: lacy means trimmed with lace
the number written as a word, not a cross-reference

explanation.surface: A racy rating for a ten in frilly lingerie that is not explicit.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' looks like a reference to 10-across, but here it is just the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Latency is the state of being hidden or present but not yet shown.

clue.text: Order fresh, crisp beer

indicators.note: a fresh version is a new one, so the letters are made over

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A pub customer asks for a cold, refreshing lager.
explanation.definitionFit: Doctors prescribe treatment, meaning they order or direct it.

clue.text: First mark made on page of official document

definitions.meaning: first meaning: occurring at the beginning

definitions.text: mark made on page of official document
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the letters of one's name written to approve each sheet

explanation.surface: The first mark you make on each page of a legal contract.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for beginning and a verb for signing with abbreviated letters.

clue.text: Drake set off with raft during the night

indicators.note: set off suggests being launched and scattered, so the letters are moved about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sir Francis Drake sailed away on a raft under cover of darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: After dark means once night has fallen, so during the nighttime.

clue.text: Lover boy Knut sporting little jumper

indicators.note: sporting means wearing, so one part is worn inside the other

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo
the setter Knut refers to himself

explanation.surface: The setter, a romantic sort, wears a little sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' tempts as a British sweater; here it is a kangaroo. A setter's own name means ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young lover gives his name to any ardent male suitor.

clue.text: Draw son disembarking sailing vessel

indicators.note: disembarking means getting off, so the letter for son leaves the word

parts.note: to draw is to sketch

explanation.surface: A father draws his son stepping ashore from a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: S is the abbreviation for son.
explanation.definitionFit: A ketch is a two-masted sailing boat with the mizzen forward of the rudder.

clue.text: Ordinary pieces which are published in the papers

definitions.text: which are published in the papers
definitions.note: a relative clause standing for the noun: things which are published

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for ordinary, as in O level
bits are small pieces

explanation.surface: Routine articles that appear in the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: Obits, short for obituaries, are death notices printed in newspapers.

clue.text: Solo Fed agent's guessing game

parts.note: Han Solo is the smuggler in Star Wars
a G-man is an FBI agent, a government man

explanation.surface: A lone FBI agent plays a game of guessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solo' looks like 'alone' but is the Star Wars surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangman is the pencil game of guessing a word letter by letter before a stick figure is drawn.

clue.text: In pursuit of time, becoming sick

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
ailing means falling ill

explanation.surface: Someone chasing time while falling ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Tailing someone is following them closely, as a detective does.

clue.text: Beginning to read Henry McDonald, a seedy crime writer

indicators.note: seedy means shabby and run down, so these letters are knocked out of shape
beginning to keeps just the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of read
taken as written

explanation.surface: Starting to read a sleazy thriller by an author called Henry McDonald.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote the hardboiled detective novels featuring Philip Marlowe.
